Tasks below are history.

phases.title: Execution contract and reproducible checks
phases.outcome: Before changing code, the actual commands, resource boundaries, and evidence format are defined.

phases.title: R14: resumable reading and a single pending-body store
phases.outcome: An ordinary paid receiver survives a Work change and cold restart, then passes the unchanged Diagnostic32 and Full130.

phases.title: Storage and the cost of long life
phases.outcome: History growth does not cause rewriting of the whole profile and does not break compatibility after an upgrade.

phases.title: Continuous payment and authority lifecycle
phases.outcome: The chat continues paid operations after epoch changes, authority updates, and a long L2 outage.

phases.title: First contact with an offline recipient
phases.outcome: The first Welcome and subsequent application messages are delivered without the sender being present.

phases.title: Autonomous recovery of ten replicas
phases.outcome: Operators restore data and indexes 10→7→10 with clients shut down and a finite budget.

phases.title: Attachments, TTL, and garbage collection
phases.outcome: Attachments are transferred in parts, resumed, and deleted under verifiable retention without plaintext leakage.

phases.title: Devices, delegation, and safe backup
phases.outcome: Profile recovery and device change do not restore revoked rights and do not clone active ratchets.

phases.title: Groups and epoch-aware recovery
phases.outcome: Real groups have roles, consistent encrypted control, safe rejoin, and two paid privacy profiles.

phases.title: Shared client API and agent operation
phases.outcome: UI, shipped CLI, and MCP show the same data and verify current limited rights.

phases.title: Transport economics of the testnet
phases.outcome: Postage stamps, subsidy, royalty, and payouts are backed by resources and do not grant control rights to fee recipients.

phases.title: Voluntary external account verification
phases.outcome: Google, Telegram, and site/org credentials grant only explicitly accepted claims; funded onboarding is limited by the campaign.

phases.title: Network and operator mode
phases.outcome: A clean client joins an independent network, communicates behind NAT, and respects resource boundaries under attacks.

phases.title: Everyday desktop
phases.outcome: The user can use chat, search, notifications, and recovery through the ordinary interface.

phases.title: Local IPC and delivery on three OSes
phases.outcome: A single Rust runtime, CLI/MCP, and Tauri work on macOS ARM64, Windows x64, and Linux x64 with private local IPC.

phases.title: Protocol compatibility and independent release preparation
phases.outcome: Before RC there is a full wire corpus, an approved testnet manifest, and a genuinely executable release runner.

phases.title: Full acceptance of a single revision
phases.outcome: All 67 cards, 22 E2E tests, 11 suites, and three OSes are accepted on a single RC; missing results block the release.

tasks.title: Link card acceptance to executable checks
steps: Cross-check this plan against release-scope and the current capability matrix; separate historical PASS from the current one.
For each future check, pin a task/E2E ID, test symbol, fixture, non-zero expected count, and evidence owner.
Extend the existing report with a missing/failed/skipped-required check and the exact revision; do not create a second backlog.
scenarios: A missing required card or a mismatched binary hash forbid product_validated.
An old successful report remains available but does not close the new revision.
tasks.acceptance: All 67/22/3 and 11 suites have a path to a mandatory verifiable result; no V2 card has become a V1 dependency.

tasks.title: Separate targeted native checks from the full release runner
steps: Take apart scripts/check-native.mjs: right now it invokes the entire scripts/check.sh.
Extract the selection of an existing targeted scenario without an implicit full suite; keep the full mode for the end of the plan.
In all modes, keep build-storage, fingerprints, exit status, and cleanup.
scenarios: The selected native case runs exactly once and does not start the workspace suite.
An empty set, an unknown case, and an erroneous child exit do not become PASS.
tasks.acceptance: There are precise documented commands for targeted native cases; the full runner still gathers all mandatory results.

tasks.title: Pin down a reproducible fault manifest
steps: Reuse the existing clock/RNG and process fixtures; describe seed, topology, ports, profiles, and kill/SQL fault points.
Persist the faults that actually fired and the hashes of original messages as a separate oracle.
Add replay for one real offline/reorder/crash scenario without an LLM dependency.
scenarios: A single seed yields the same set of fault transitions and final MessageIDs.
A kill/SQL trigger that did not fire or a lost log make the result incomplete.
tasks.acceptance: Replay verifies production reducers and the durable result; virtual time is not passed off as elapsed native time.

tasks.title: Fix the resource and trust model of the V1 testnet
steps: Consolidate the effective byte/entry/CPU/read/retention/queue limits and the source of each parameter.
Tie the paid classes, R=10, minimum copies, repair reserve, subsidy, and royalty to the conservation model.
Describe the chosen L2/checkpoint profile, quorum assumptions, and failure domains; leave undetermined monetary values as explicit decisions until the economic implementation.
scenarios: An example of one send, index, read, and repair fits within the paid resource without a second postage stamp for the index.
A shortage of fund/capacity or a hard lease expiry yields a bounded refusal, not a new resource.
tasks.acceptance: A versioned manifest distinguishes protocol limits, rig parameters, and monetary decisions not yet adopted; there is no hidden TTL increase.
tasks.external_dependency: Confirmed testnet parameters, subsidy budget, fee, and payouts; until they are chosen, the monetary gate cannot be declared satisfied.

tasks.title: Build a fast diagnostic loop and a reproducer with controlled time
steps: In the native run harness, add selection of a targeted diagnostic phase, a budget for lack of useful progress, and early stop with a full state snapshot (page identity, revision, manifest hash, ACK set, data/index receipts, capacity/error counter deltas; for H11 — exact inbox MessageIDs, recipient cursor/deferred, custodySync, the exact SQL fault event; import of previous originals and the exact fault shown separately).
Extend historyDiagnostics with a retry schedule and a series of snapshots; after the sender shuts down in H11, show the main expected work.

Introduce a "clocks + timers + events" seam with four time loops (protocol, scheduler monotonic, chain, real execution); complete the unfinished _at seams in maintain_public_sender_at, paid_custody, and the embedded finalizer service.

Assemble a sender/custody/history reproducer: several logical nodes in one process, production transitions, controlled message delivery, real SQLCipher, controlled RNG and completion order; virtual time advances to the nearest event only after accounting for all earlier ones.
Hook up Anvil as a separate adapter (set timestamp → produce a block → get result → continue the scenario).
Check and remove extra pauses after dependencies are ready: wake work by event without weakening mandatory backoff/admission limits.
Run the full unchanged A04/H11 on a fix candidate; initiate renewal for diagnostics with the existing maintain(force=True) without scaling the lease/series of the scenario.
scenarios: An early stop returns "observation received" or "suspected stall" with a full snapshot and is not passed off as a PASS of the full scenario.
A single seed yields the same event trace and reproducer digest; hidden use of wall clock, nondeterministic RNG, or the real network is caught by a negative check.
The reproducer repeats the real failure class within minutes while preserving meaningful load and real SQL fault boundaries.
Unchanged native A04/H11 confirm the fix; simulated elapsed time in evidence is separated from native elapsed time.
tasks.acceptance: A diagnostic iteration of the selected phase completes within minutes with a saved snapshot; the reproducer drives production sender/custody/history under shared controlled time; no acceptance parameter was changed for speed. Full F03 remains with V1-V03; QEMU icount is a separate experiment.

tasks.title: Close two gaps in Node range continuation tests
steps: Keep the six already written runtime tests and the real paid Noise fixtures; do not change production yet.
Add an empty advancing page: 33 originals, the first 32 expired, the last one alive; the actual response with after=0 contains next=32 in the absence of bodies.
Add complete=true below the selected missing: the holder still has originals 1–2, the current history requires 4; after a cold Core the request must be exact after=3.
Verify the durable cursor, MLS immutability until import, and the actual next request; obtain an independent final ACCEPT of the tests.
scenarios: Removing next_sequence from the result breaks the first scenario after a cold open.
Ignoring complete breaks exact repair; a complete from one holder does not close the whole history.
Fixtures keep the ordinary request limit, real receipts, the current root/epoch, and a real loss of SQL rows.
tasks.acceptance: Both previously blocking REVISE remarks are closed with discriminating tests; compile/behavioral RED and a separate ACCEPT are preserved. Compilation passing by itself does not count as behavioral RED.

tasks.title: Preserve the boundaries of the verified paid page
steps: First adapt the existing obligation/prefix/binding tests to the common range contract and run the critic gate.
Return verified envelopes, next_sequence, and complete from the whole-page verifier; keep the verification of every late proof before any staging.
Allow after below the selected sequence with the same binding to operation/index/epoch; forbid substituting the holder, order, and budget.
scenarios: A valid first body and a corrupted second one do not save anything.
An empty range with skipped expired slots saves next; foreign index/epoch, next going backwards, and exceeding the proof budget are rejected.
tasks.acceptance: The verifier yields a single verified page result without losing continuation; wire/admission limits and historical paid checks are preserved.

tasks.title: Wire durable range into the ordinary Runtime
steps: Choose after via the Core custody_prefetch_after immediately before the real request and keep the exact current head in Pending.
Apply the response through an atomic Core range API; re-verify the current head/time/authority on apply.
Continue with the same holder only on full staging, an incomplete page, and the need for the next range; on capacity, move on without repeating an unchanged page.
scenarios: A real Work expires, Core opens from disk, a new request continues after=2 without re-fetching the prefix.
A pointer change under the same root and a marker SQL failure save bodies/cursor/MLS together or change nothing.
With 127 cached bodies, a response with two new ones does not advance the cursor and does not loop the holder.
tasks.acceptance: New H01 and the existing six runtime scenarios are green through the ordinary queue, Noise, paid verification, and Core; the import goes through the common receive boundary.

tasks.title: Remove the temporary prefix-ledger and keep read compatibility
steps: Reduce Prefix/Obligation to a single range mode; remove per-Work PrefixReads and the duplicate checker branches.
Keep the order of route classes; if priority for unread holders is needed, take it from the durable Core, not from a new temporary map.
Keep legacy for the existing non-history locator; a generic failure does not return a legacy fallback. Align the trace kind with the parser.
scenarios: A new Work does not make a previously read holder new.
Capacity/unavailable/rejected/transport failures move to the next holder; the old non-history locator reads the original ciphertext.
The 129th holder does not displace durable progress and does not disappear from the candidate list.
tasks.acceptance: One range path, the former negative/legacy controls, and the parser are green; there is no separate diagnostic RPC.

tasks.title: Carry an unfinished root proof between Work items
steps: Find the part of Flow that loses the unfinished traversal and use the existing durable graph cursor/cache.
Persist only bounded verified pages and the exact head/root/source; do not serialize network streams or the whole Runtime.
On cold resume, re-verify the mutable authority/expiry/head and continue the missing branches.
scenarios: A kill after receiving part of the branch proof does not force rereading already saved pages from scratch.
A new pointer/epoch and an SQL failure do not join incompatible proof fragments; a finished result after the deadline is verified before releasing the Work.
tasks.acceptance: A bounded incomplete proof survives Work/cold restart without a false complete and without increasing the 120 seconds/16 visits.

tasks.title: Specify a compatible unified pending-body schema
steps: Describe the operation key with binding to conversation/index/epoch, the single body, and the reasons for waiting on import.
Write fixtures for both former prefetch/deferred formats, their intersection, and cold migration.
Preserve the combined capacity of the two old stores: 128+128 entries and 4+4 MiB of bodies; account for metadata/proofs separately.
scenarios: One ciphertext present in both old caches becomes a single entry without losing the fresher valid context.
Conflicting bytes of one operation are rejected; filled distinct old caches are not truncated to a single limit of 128.
tasks.acceptance: The format contract, SQL fault tests, compatibility fixtures, and ACCEPT exist before the production migration.

tasks.title: Unify persistence and migration of pending bodies
steps: Introduce one persisted representation in the current ProfileStore/Core without a third cache.
Move the prefetch/deferred producers to shared admission with dedup and the former combined budget.
Perform the forward migration atomically; the reader of old rows remains until a successful commit and a cold check.
scenarios: A kill/SQL fault in the middle of migration leaves either the old readable state or the new one entirely.
Repeating an already imported original does not return it to pending; exceeding capacity does not advance the scan marker.
tasks.acceptance: A body is stored once, former pending originals are available after restart, quotas and original signatures are preserved.

tasks.title: Make gap retry dependent on real progress
steps: Tie the repeat of decrypt/import to a change in relevant MLS state, root, or the exact body.
Order attempts by the authenticated sender stream/epoch, not by the global group sequence.
Continue fetching subsequent bodies on a gap; put an SQL failure on its own retry, do not wait for an MLS change.
scenarios: An unchanged ratchet gap does not trigger repeated SQL/crypto attempts on every tick.
The appearance of the missing message triggers sequential imports; another sender is not blocked.
After the SQL trigger is lifted, the same ciphertext is imported without a new MLS event.
tasks.acceptance: There is no infinite gap rotation; message/MLS/import record/pending removal/recovery progress are committed in a single receive_verified_with_states transaction.

tasks.title: Run the targeted R14 integration cluster
steps: Run the changed range/import/worker/legacy/admission/backend clusters and the related frontend recovery views.
Verify the cold upgrade of the former profile and the exact rollback/import IDs; finish Clippy/fmt for the affected crates.
Save critic verdicts, commands, duration, failed candidates, source/config hashes, and the conclusion about the boundaries of the result.
scenarios: The targeted reversed-130 import confirms all real messages, not a cache union.
A zero test sample, stale binaries, or a failed negative control forbid ACCEPT.
tasks.acceptance: There is a current component checkpoint for H01–H08; it is not directly called a native Full130 pass.

tasks.title: Match Diagnostic32 against the unchanged baseline
steps: Use the ordinary CLI/Core and a single trace scheme reference→request→response→staging→import/rollback.
Perform 32 publications, real 288+288 losses, sender absent, trust refusal, both SQL faults, partial/full/cold at the former deadlines.
Compare leaf occupancy, new/repeated reads, the number of admitted requests, and wall time with output/hrt32-r1; distinguish causes by the facts of the trace.
scenarios: The SQL fault actually fires on the expected original; the imported count and the plaintext oracle match.
A reduction in reads is not accepted at the cost of losing bodies, late expiry, or raised allowances.
tasks.acceptance: The full Diagnostic32 passes or yields a localized blocker; halving the reads is a verifiable efficiency hypothesis, not a substitute for correctness.

tasks.title: Close out the unchanged Full130 and the Native20 control
steps: Build the exact candidate binaries and pin the source gates before the run.
Verify 130 paid originals, 390 signatures, 1300 data/1300 index and 13000 location ACKs; delete the real 1170+1170 copies and remove the sender.
Pass missing trust, first rollback, partial129, last rollback, full130, and cold full graph up to the original earliest expiry; match the Native20 R10 control.
scenarios: All 130 exact messages are available regardless of temporary caches and the current sender.
Neither TTL 3600, deadlines, nor read/CPU/storage limits change for the sake of a PASS; all processes are stopped and temporary keys deleted.
tasks.acceptance: Full native evidence exists on unchanged inputs/binaries; R13/R14 failures are preserved. Otherwise D05 remains open with the cause measured.

tasks.title: Introduce a single profile version and atomic forward migrations
steps: Inventory the existing schema and versioned state namespaces without renaming all modules.
Add a common schema version and an explicit supported-read/write envelope; provide a verifiable backup before an irreversible migration.
Apply migrations in a single transaction/in stages with a resumable marker; forbid silent reset and running an old writer on the new schema.
scenarios: An old profile is upgraded with the same identity, outbox, MLS, and grants.
Kill/disk-full/wrong-key do not create an empty new profile; rollback restores the consistent old state.
tasks.acceptance: There are production upgrade/reopen tests for the whole profile, not just a single JSON namespace.

tasks.title: Eliminate re-storing of immutable proof bundles
steps: Measure the repeated paid proof bytes by book/authority/QC in real rows.
Reuse the content-addressed immutable proof record and references from obligations where already verified bytes are available.
Migrate without changing the signed wire; GC deletes a proof only after the last live reference and admissible retention.
scenarios: Different operations of one book are read after a cold restart via the original proof bytes.
A missing/substituted bundle is not considered verified; an SQL fault does not leave a dangling reference.
tasks.acceptance: Bytes before/after and bounded lookup are measured; historical retrieval does not depend on the active wallet or a new checkpoint.

tasks.title: Move to incremental transactional MLS persistence
steps: Profile the current MLS store snapshot on a typical send/receive; select the actually changed keys/rows.
Embed the incremental provider into the existing Core transaction instead of independent writers.
Preserve the in-memory MLS rollback together with the SQL rollback and a cold read of the old profile.
scenarios: Send/receive/retry across several dialogs change only the necessary records and keep an identical transcript.
A failure of the last SQL write does not save the new ratchet separately from the message/outbox.
tasks.acceptance: The number of rewritten bytes is bounded by the change; the atomic model and recovery are verified, and the measurement is compared with the baseline.

tasks.title: Bound expensive immutable verification outside the Core writer
steps: From the trace, isolate the genuinely blocking pure checks while keeping the already existing opaque validated tokens.
Hook bounded execution slots/completion events into the existing processing budget; do not create independent mutable Core.
On commit, re-verify the current grant/trust/time/connection and CAS the original bytes; cancellation frees the slot.
scenarios: A heavy honest/hostile peer does not block owner IPC and another dialog beyond the stated budget.
Revocation, pointer/epoch change, and disconnect before the worker finishes reject a stale result; memory is bounded.
tasks.acceptance: Improvement is measured on the real bottleneck and security fences are preserved. If the baseline already fits, a documented no-change with this evidence is acceptable.

tasks.title: Automatically obtain and refresh an admissible authority
steps: Connect the existing checkpoint refresh with ordinary client/finalizer discovery and an explicitly accepted trust profile.
Persist the trusted authority and cursor atomically; cut off a false source, a stale epoch, and an incompatible chain lineage.
Remove the need for manual owner commands from routine renewal.
scenarios: A clean client with accepted trust obtains the authority and sends, then continues after renewal/cold restart.
A conspiracy of several RPCs without valid checkpoint signatures does not create an authority; an SQL fault leaves the previous consistent state.
tasks.acceptance: Renewal passes in the ordinary flow with bounded retry; sources and trust assumptions are shown in evidence.

tasks.title: Close an epoch when the old authority expires
steps: Define an admissible signed closing lineage from the already existing spent history and expiry policy.
Separate historical validation of old records from the right to a new signature; do not revive an expired signer.
Load the full authenticated prefix before resolving negative membership in the successor.
scenarios: The old signer is offline/expired, but an admissible retained closing moves all spent rows into the new composition.
An incomplete prefix, a modified QC, and a replay of an old stamp do not produce a second spend.
tasks.acceptance: Epoch transfer does not reset the spent namespace; exact historical QC/readAt are preserved after a kill and cold resume.

tasks.title: Recover pending inputs after expiry and non-delivery
steps: Separate reserved, exposed stamp, final spend, and refundable in the existing job ledger.
For an unconfirmed operation, choose an admissible resume/new preparation with an idempotent operation ID and accounting for the already exposed resource.
After an authority change, re-verify the original grant and budget before a network action.
scenarios: A crash between reserve/publish/finality and authority expiry do not create two paid operations.
An exposed/final stamp is not returned to the balance; a cancelled grant does not revive after renewal.
tasks.acceptance: The user sees the exact reason for pending/expired and can continue an admissible send without an issuer reset.

tasks.title: Pin down retention for the journal of completed sends
steps: Reuse the implemented retirement and message_delivery projections; inventory the proof/evidence rows still being held.
Delete only transient completed work after durable publication, keeping original/history, claims, and mandatory paid evidence until their term.
Separate GC observation/receipt/evidence from freeing the active queue.
scenarios: Two consecutive series of more than 128 sends free active slots, while an old recipient recovers the history without the sender.
An SQL failure during retirement/GC does not return spent resource and does not delete the last discoverability reference.
tasks.acceptance: The active queue is bounded by concurrency, not lifetime; long-lived evidence has an explicit term and a measured volume.

tasks.title: Close the public/legacy verifier boundary
steps: Verify the already working ordinary public build and extract only the genuinely shared neutral funding/authority DTOs from proof-heavy dependencies.
Keep the frozen legacy relation/image IDs and separate verify/prove targets; an ordinary send does not start the prover.
Add cross-format vectors for the shared spent namespace and a strict ban on malformed public→legacy fallback.
scenarios: An old paid record is verified by the current reader after an upgrade.
A transcoded or substituted public stamp does not get a second nullifier namespace and does not trigger a fallback.
tasks.acceptance: The ordinary target is independent of the prover; historical compatibility and the explicit legacy gate are verified without regenerating the frozen proof identity.

tasks.title: Verify the long spend/renewal/outage cycle
steps: Reuse the native handover fixture: more than 128 spends, several real compositions, cold missing history, and the client returning.
Add ordinary automatic renewal, undelivered inputs, and an outage before/after the hard lease.
Preserve the supply/spent/claim invariants and independent verifier signatures.
scenarios: After hard expiry, new admissions wait, while old live retrieval keeps working.
Concurrent replay during handover does not create a second final spend; recovery does not require a manual QC install.
tasks.acceptance: There is a single-piece current-revision AR1 scenario; local 133-spend historical results do not substitute for the new gate.

tasks.title: Specify a one-time private invite and control admission
steps: Tie invite/prekey/Welcome to owner, contact, protocol version, expiry, and one-time consumption.
Use the common encrypted-object pipeline with a separate control kind before an established conversation.
Bound the public contact endpoint with a quota and exclude an open contact list.
scenarios: A valid invite admits one intended recipient and the creation of a single chat.
A foreign owner, a replay of a used prekey, an expired invite, and unsolicited flood do not create MLS state.
tasks.acceptance: The signed wire contract and tests are accepted before production; custodians do not receive MLS secrets.

tasks.title: Persist and publish a paid Welcome
steps: Include the Welcome in the existing durable outbox/public sender with a separate admissible control resource.
Atomically persist the contact intent, control envelope, reservation, and subsequent publication.
Publish a discoverable private rendezvous and receipts until the sender's retirement.
scenarios: The sender completes the first contact while Bob is offline and leaves; the Welcome remains available.
A kill between MLS preparation, outbox, and receipt does not lose the Welcome and does not spend a second stamp.
tasks.acceptance: Control does not require an already established chat and is not served by a free unlimited channel.

tasks.title: Import the Welcome and continue the application history
steps: Receive only the addressed private control through the ordinary discovery/custody path.
Verify invite/owner/expiry, create MLS/contact and the consumption marker atomically.
After commit, move to the ordinary paid application history; a duplicate Welcome is idempotent.
scenarios: The Welcome arrives after some application bodies: saved bodies are imported after MLS is established.
An SQL fault on the Welcome and a cold retry do not create a second chat; replay/foreign control does not modify the profile.
tasks.acceptance: The recipient does not require a live sender and does not import application into an unconfirmed contact.

tasks.title: Accept the first offline DM via UI and CLI
steps: Create two clean profiles through the ordinary entry points; Bob is offline until the first invite/Welcome.
Send a known first text, remove Alice and some holders, turn on Bob, then repeat the cold cycle.
Verify plaintext/MessageID, costs, contact state, and error state on both adapters.
scenarios: The first message is available exactly once without sources, raw owner RPC, or a manually imported Welcome.
An incorrect invitation and a lack of paid control budget give an honest refusal.
tasks.acceptance: There is a real-process vertical of first contact; the established-chat smoke is saved separately.

tasks.title: Persist real repair obligations and probes
steps: Derive repair obligations from the existing paid receipts, placement, and retention; do not create a global repair consensus.
In a single bounded scheduler for data/index, keep probe due time, the actual result, attempt, and the final deadline.
Verify the presence of ciphertext/hash, not just peer availability or the number of signatures.
scenarios: A vanished assigned copy becomes degraded after the confirmed policy of probes.
A brief timeout is not treated as proof of malice; duplicate probes do not multiply jobs.
tasks.acceptance: The repair queue survives a daemon restart and is bounded by paid obligations/resources.

tasks.title: Select and authorize a replacement holder
steps: Reuse the authenticated registry snapshot, placement proofs, and the already paid copy allowance.
Pin a bounded repair responsibility/lease with fencing so several operators do not spend one quota indefinitely.
Select admissible spare nodes accounting for capacity and the end of the original lease; updating the composition does not extend the TTL.
scenarios: Two operators notice the same loss simultaneously: the result is consistent and the costs are finite.
A foreign holder, stale assignment, replayed lease, and absence of reserve do not yield a paid copy.
tasks.acceptance: Every replacement copy has a verifiable basis and does not require the sender's signer.

tasks.title: Copy the ciphertext and update discoverability atomically
steps: Fetch the original/copy from a surviving holder with historical proof validation.
Issue a new receipt only after the durable commit of bytes on the spare.
Through the existing index/location pipeline, publish the new locations and keep stage progress until the repair job retires.
scenarios: A process loss between data copy, receipt, and location ACK is recovered without a false R10.
A substituted blob, an incomplete page, or an SQL failure do not update the available copy count.
tasks.acceptance: An independent audit client finds and reads the new bytes via the index; both roles are served by a shared scheduler.

tasks.title: Bound storm, exhausted capacity, and repair GC
steps: Build per-peer/global backoff and fair scheduling into the existing admission/processing budgets.
When spare/funds are absent, keep degraded and a verifiable reason; do not re-sign a promise without resource.
Finish repair on expiry, keeping evidence until settlement and deleting only admissible transient rows.
scenarios: Mass node loss does not displace an honest DM from the bounded queues.
A repeated restart does not reset budget/backoff; an expired obligation is neither repaired nor extended.
tasks.acceptance: CPU/network/disk and costs are measured under burst; the actual durability is shown to the user.

tasks.title: Prove autonomous data/index 10→7→10
steps: Bring up 10 assigned and spare identities, send known objects, and verify the original copies.
Shut down both clients and three assigned storage profiles; confirm the processes and the inventory loss.
Wait for operator-only repair, read the new ciphertext/index from a separate auditor, and bring the recipient back. Repeat the branch without spares.
scenarios: The new copies have the original hashes, valid receipts, and locations; Bob receives the original message.
Without spares, the UI stays degraded rather than showing a restored ten.
tasks.acceptance: The native repair vertical with a finite cost is closed; the counts of identities/processes/machines/operators are listed separately.

tasks.title: Define the encrypted chunk/manifest contract
steps: Specify a bounded manifest with hashes, count, sizes, encryption context, and expiry.
Bind the manifest to the message, owner/grant, and the payable class; separate read and repair capabilities.
Add vectors for a valid attachment and reject cases before production; take the concrete fields/limits from the shared wire/resource manifest.
scenarios: The assembled chunks reproduce the original file byte-for-byte.
Substituted order/hash/size, a foreign context, and an oversized manifest are rejected before expensive decode.
tasks.acceptance: One versioned format, a clear price, and bounded memory; there is no new unbounded blob service.

tasks.title: Implement resumable chunk upload
steps: Encrypt/read the file in a streaming fashion inside the trusted backend; the renderer gets progress without the keys.
Persist manifest/chunk upload progress in the transactional outbox and place it through the shared paid store.
Retry only the missing chunks, preserving operation identity and budget.
scenarios: A restart after some receipts continues from the needed chunk without paying a second time.
Cancellation/a foreign grant/full disk does not publish a completed attachment and leaves no plaintext temp.
tasks.acceptance: Bounded placement of a large file works on cold retry and does not load the whole file into memory.

tasks.title: Implement download/resume with final verification
steps: Download the missing permitted chunks by the bounded manifest with shared fetch/admission.
Persist encrypted partial progress; before handing over the file, verify all hashes and the total size.
Pass the renderer a safe user-selected file handle/path; do not execute the content or an active preview.
scenarios: Network/relay loss and a cold restart continue the exact parts; the final hash matches.
A single wrong chunk does not become a ready attachment; traversal/an unsafe name does not write outside the chosen destination.
tasks.acceptance: The UI receives truthful progress/retry/error; completed means verified bytes.

tasks.title: Tie retention/GC to live leases and repair
steps: Reuse the shared GC scheduler for chunk/manifest/proof rows.
Hold ciphertext until the paid expiry and live references; verify repair rights separately from read.
On quota/disk-full, choose refusing a new admission, not destroying valid paid data.
scenarios: Before the TTL, an attachment is recovered after holder loss; after the TTL, retrieval is no longer promised.
A kill during GC and a shared manifest of several recipients do not delete a still-needed chunk/proof.
tasks.acceptance: Retained usage and actual bytes agree after a cold restart; the absence of resource is reflected in the status.

tasks.title: Add user-facing file sending and saving
steps: Build a file picker, upload/download progress, cancel/retry, and save into the current ChatShell.
Price/TTL are confirmed by the same wallet/budget flow; do not duplicate backend eligibility.
Verify keyboard/accessibility, a malicious filename/preview, and visually inspect the saved headless screenshots.
scenarios: The user sends a file, restarts the application, and continues the download.
A storage/permission error stays on the specific attachment and does not break text chat.
tasks.acceptance: UI and CLI use a single attachment service; component and native checks confirm the final hash.

tasks.title: Complete the device/org grant policy
steps: Extend the existing capabilities only with the missing device/org constraints, tying owner/device epochs together.
Verify methods, contacts/groups, TTL, budget, and delegation depth in the shared broker before an action and when resuming a job.
Make revoke atomic with the change of the relevant fences; do not refresh independent UI copies of rights.
scenarios: Admissible devices and two runtimes operate within their own limits.
An old epoch, a widening child grant, and a revocation between prepare/commit forbid the action without returning the spent budget.
tasks.acceptance: One authorization matrix covers UI/CLI/MCP, devices, and the organizational messaging budget.

tasks.title: Bind a device to the identity and MLS leaf
steps: Confirm a new device with a bounded owner/recovery challenge and proof of possession.
Persist the device key/NetworkID/MLS leaf binding and the key package lifecycle.
Revoking a device forbids future actions and requires an admissible MLS epoch transition; do not promise deletion of already received plaintext.
scenarios: A person with two devices receives the permitted messages without mixing the human identity and the leaves.
Repeated onboarding, a foreign device key, and a stale owner challenge do not attach a device.
tasks.acceptance: There is a real device join/remove and cold state; future group integration uses this shared service.

tasks.title: Define a versioned encrypted backup
steps: Compose a single consistency snapshot of identity/contacts/history/MLS/outbox/grants without writing plaintext to temp/logs.
Define the envelope version, integrity, password/recovery-key encryption, and compatibility rules.
Choose a safe restore: transfer/rejoin with new device state instead of cloning two active ratchets/spend writers.
scenarios: A backup after restart contains a consistent slice of messages and pending operations.
A wrong password, truncation, and an unsupported critical version are rejected without changing the working profile.
tasks.acceptance: There are format fixtures and an independent test ACCEPT; the antirollback authority policy is written down explicitly.

tasks.title: Implement atomic export and validated import
steps: Create the encrypted export in a user-chosen location with bounded IO and atomic completion.
Validate the import in a separate temporary profile, then switch to the intact result.
On an incompatible schema, apply S01; do not carry over local active IPC tokens as new authorizations.
scenarios: Export/import restores texts, contacts, and admissible state onto a clean profile.
Disk-full/a kill at the end of export or import preserves the original working profile and does not report a successful backup.
tasks.acceptance: The backup is fit for cold restore; secret temporary files and transient keys are deleted after completion.

tasks.title: Verify current authorizations after an old backup
steps: On restore, recover current ownership/revocation/checkpoint floors from admissible history.
Do not treat old grants/spent snapshots as grounds for new spending or the return of a revoked device.
If a fresh authority is unavailable, allow safe local reading and show pending/rejoin-required for forbidden actions.
scenarios: An old backup after a revoke does not bring back rights; a replay of an old stamp is not spent.
No authoritative fresh data: the profile does not automatically start signing with new copies of the old MLS/spend state.
tasks.acceptance: Antirollback is verified with a real old backup and a separate live profile.

tasks.title: Verify the keystore and cleanup of temporary test keys
steps: Check the ordinary system keystore, profile encryption, and E2eFileStore across the supported OSes.
For automatic native tests, use only debug/e2e and a temporary profile; ensure cleanup after normal/error/kill.
Confirm the feature boundary: the production artifact does not contain the test selection of the file-keystore.
scenarios: Repeated native runs do not touch the login Keychain and do not trigger a password prompt.
A cleanup failure is recorded; a wrong key for the production profile yields a refusal, not a reset.
tasks.acceptance: Automation is isolated from system keys. The real system_keychain_roundtrip remains a separate explicitly permitted interactive gate.

tasks.title: Add group intents and a role matrix
steps: Introduce domain commands create/invite/join/leave/remove with a human/device distinction.
Tie the signed intent to group_id, the final parent epoch, and the current role grant.
Use the MLS adapter for keys, the shared broker for policy, and the atomic outbox for control.
scenarios: Owner/admin/member have explicitly different admissible operations.
A former admin, a foreign group invite, and an unconfirmed device do not change the roster.
tasks.acceptance: A group is created by the ordinary application service; no endpoint bypasses the role checks.

tasks.title: Persist encrypted control payload until finality
steps: Publish control ciphertext through the shared paid custody/index pipeline with retention and receipts.
Reconcile only commitment/order metadata; do not pass MLS secrets to the finalizer.
Do not allow finalization before sufficient verified persistence of the payload under the accepted contract.
scenarios: With an offline participant, retained control can be fetched from other holders.
A withheld payload or a receipt without saved bytes does not become the final control step.
tasks.acceptance: The final control entry references available verified ciphertext; the work does not require a single administrator to be online.

tasks.title: Wire BFT ordering into the group control log
steps: Reuse the generic finalizer for control, not for every application message.
Separate the ordering of proposals from the verification of MLS semantics by recipients.
Apply an admissible final entry in a single transaction with the epoch/control cursor; preserve safety under partition.
scenarios: A 4/3 committee under a 2/2 partition does not finalize new state; after recovery, a common prefix.
A modified parent/QC or two conflicting final entries are not accepted.
tasks.acceptance: Real processes converge to a single control prefix without lowering the quorum.

tasks.title: Handle concurrent MLS commits and deterministic reject
steps: Build a commit only from an accepted final parent; re-evaluate losing intents on the new epoch.
Define a single reject/no-op for finalized ciphertext with inadmissible MLS semantics.
After a locally accepted Remove, do not encrypt new sensitive messages into the old epoch; do not roll back used ratchets.
scenarios: Add+Remove, Remove+Update, and two device joins yield the same roster on all honest clients.
A malicious steward and an invalid MLS commit do not create a fork or key reuse; a removed leaf cannot read the new epoch.
tasks.acceptance: Safety and decryptability are verified with real OpenMLS on conflicting traces, not only by consensus state.

tasks.title: Recover control and application across epochs
steps: Read retained control and the application messages belonging to it in an order that preserves the admissible key window.
Process the messages of an epoch before deleting the needed keys; do not keep keys forever.
With an incomplete legacy/control range, show an explicit gap/rejoin-required and continue the permitted work.
scenarios: Being offline longer than three past epochs recovers within the retained data or gets an exact boundary of the inaccessible.
Applying all new commits does not silently destroy the only keys to still-available messages; a forged snapshot is rejected.
tasks.acceptance: There is a real multi-epoch catch-up, an explicit partial result, and a safe transition past the retention window.

tasks.title: Perform an authorized device rejoin and history sharing
steps: Request a rejoin under the current membership/recovery grants and create new device/MLS secrets.
Restore only admissible retained messages; make transferring old history to a new participant a separate authorized action.
Persist rejoin progress/Welcome consumption atomically and retry after an SQL failure.
scenarios: A lost device is replaced, and the remaining participants continue the chat.
A revoked device and a former participant do not use backup/rejoin to regain rights; a new participant does not get old secrets by default.
tasks.acceptance: Rejoin does not clone an active ratchet and does not hide the loss of inaccessible history.

tasks.title: Enable the shared-group-storage profile
steps: Store a single encrypted application blob with admissible group read/repair rights.
Account for the fanout of several participants/devices in the price/resource manifest.
Tie membership changes to future read capabilities without promising to erase previously received content.
scenarios: Permitted participants read the same ciphertext through the shared store.
Quota/an excluded recipient and a stale capability do not yield new paid reads.
tasks.acceptance: The profile and the disclosed storage metadata are documented; the actual cost is verified.

tasks.title: Enable the private-recipient-pointers profile
steps: Use the same E2EE bodies with separate secret recipient pointers and bounded discovery.
Do not include an open roster in the pointers; account for the cost of each permitted fanout.
Provide pointer/manifest repair without widening access.
scenarios: A lost portion of pointers is recovered for the permitted recipients.
A foreign recipient does not get a lookup capability; the link of the same blob/time is not declared hidden from a global observer.
tasks.acceptance: Both profiles pass the same content-secrecy check and a separate metadata-boundary check.

tasks.title: Add an organizational group and a shared messaging budget
steps: Tie a permanent org group to the membership policy and a shared finite postage budget.
Delegate separate runtime limits without transferring the treasury/master key; do not include V2 jobs/order rooms.
On revoke/archive, keep the history and the already spent budget while stopping new actions.
scenarios: Two agents simultaneously spend their limits from the shared fund without overspend.
A guest of one group does not read other org conversations; revoke/restart does not return the spending.
tasks.acceptance: Organizational messaging works through the shared grant/budget primitives, without a new job engine.

tasks.title: Add UI for groups, devices, and privacy selection
steps: Add create/invite/roles/device list/remove/rejoin and explicit privacy selection to the current shell.
Show pending membership until finality, the real metadata/cost differences of the profiles, and the boundaries of history sharing.
Verify keyboard flows and headless screenshots; native actions must invoke the shared Rust service.
scenarios: The user creates a group, adds a second device, excludes a participant, and recovers after being offline.
A quorum/storage failure does not look like a completed removal; a dangerous expansion of history requires a specific user action.
tasks.acceptance: There is usable UI for the whole group vertical with actual verification of keys/roster, not just screenshots.

tasks.title: Complete the shared delivery/read/durability model
steps: Reconcile the already persisted orthogonal funding/delivery/storage/discovery/work projections across all adapters.
Add the missing durable read/ack lifecycle per actor and inbox without duplicating business logic in TS.
Preserve the admissible state "delivered, stored 4/10" and an explanation of partial/gap.
scenarios: CLI/MCP/desktop return the same snapshot for an exact message ID after a restart.
A read ACK does not become an R10 storage proof; a storage receipt does not mean the recipient has read it.
tasks.acceptance: A single persisted projection and a stable typed contract cover the whole messaging lifecycle.

tasks.title: Add inbox leases and outbox fencing for several runtimes
steps: Use the existing poll/ack and runtime grant IDs for a finite lease of one message/stream.
Fence outgoing actions of the old runtime after takeover; deduct shared messaging budgets atomically.
Survive pause/revoke/restart without losing the unread inbox; job execution/cancel/result remain V2.
scenarios: Two runtimes do not acknowledge each other's leased inbox and do not repeat a fenced send.
A crash of the lease owner yields a permitted takeover after the term; the old actor does not return via retry.
tasks.acceptance: Switching host/runtime preserves message delivery and budget; external side effects are not declared exactly-once.

tasks.title: Reconcile the default V1 API/tool catalog
steps: Keep messaging, grants, wallet/network/recovery in the default UI/CLI/MCP; hide V2 jobs/services/reviews behind the existing feature/capability boundary.
Simplify only the duplicate DTOs and adapters around the shared typed service; do not reorganize the whole workspace.
Pin down the supported same-UID host trust model and the scope limits of the delegated handle.
scenarios: Default tools are available by grant and do not offer V2 operations.
Historical V2 readers/tests are preserved; a forged scoped request does not gain root capability.
tasks.acceptance: The default delivery matches the V1 scope; same-UID processes are not declared an isolated sandbox that does not exist.

tasks.title: Complete the grants panel and provisioning host
steps: Show runtime identity, contacts/groups/methods, limit, and term before issuing a connection context.
Provisioning returns the real packaged CLI/MCP paths and a private handle available to the chosen host.
Carry out revocation/limit change through the backend; incoming message texts cannot change the approval themselves.
scenarios: The user connects and revokes a runtime, sees the old actor's refusal after the revoke.
Changed action parameters do not use the former approval; secrets do not end up in renderer logs.
tasks.acceptance: There is a component/native UI flow and a visual check; the limits match the broker.

tasks.title: Verify the shipped CLI skill and MCP on a real host
steps: From the installed artifact, run identity/send/delivery/poll/ack under the issued context without dev APIs; include a new contact.
Repeat with an independent MCP wire client: negotiation, tools/resources, bad scopes, stdout protocol only.
Perform a real host smoke with restart/revoke and NAT/relay; if the skill changes, separately check the instruction quality per AGENTS.
scenarios: CLI works without MCP; the agent receives and acks a reply after a restart.
Malicious content does not widen scopes or provoke a forbidden send; an incompatible version is explicitly refused.
tasks.acceptance: A transcript of a real host and black-box conformance is obtained, including first contact; a deterministic fixture does not close this gate by itself.
tasks.external_dependency: An available real agent host and a separate test conversation; outgoing messages only to explicitly permitted test addressees.

tasks.title: Complete the external wallet→funded book flow
steps: Use the current public purchase flow with a real external wallet and one chosen EVM L2 testnet.
Verify exact chain/genesis/issuer, resource class, amount, confirmation/finality before funding.
Persist pending tx/reorg/retry without re-issuing tickets.
scenarios: A clean user buys a resource and sends a message through the UI without internal commands.
Wrong chain/issuer, a rejected tx, and a reorg do not create an available balance.
tasks.acceptance: Local EVM and the testnet use pinned bytecode/config domains; there are real receipts from an external wallet.
tasks.external_dependency: Testnet, a funded test account, and a compatible external wallet; real money is not required.

tasks.title: Complete the registry bond/unbond and snapshot lifecycle
steps: Verify the already implemented registry/selection and close the missing bond/unbond delays and obligation fences.
Tie the committed assignment to the future beacon and the authenticated stake snapshot.
Pin down an independent reference computation of root/count/units and admissible bias/withholding.
scenarios: New stake does not change the already selected roster; a permitted unbond does not remove a live obligation.
A stale/reorg snapshot, early withdrawal, and split identities do not bypass fixed units.
tasks.acceptance: A real testnet registry epoch is verified by clients and operators; keys and operators are not mixed in the report.

tasks.title: Implement the funded SubsidyVault and schedule
steps: Pin the campaign/global/epoch caps, cutoff/decay, and integer rounding from the accepted manifest.
Issue ordinary-format stamps only within the deposited collateral and the bounded sponsor gas.
Preserve the independent paid path after cutoff/exhaustion; do not make optional EntryBond a mandatory dependency without a separate decision.
scenarios: Time/epoch boundaries yield a continuous bounded entitlement without negative balances.
An empty fund, a replay of one claim, and a reentrant call do not create unbacked stamps.
tasks.acceptance: The conservation model and contract tests agree; there is no promise of money/cash-out for login.

tasks.title: Build atomic claim-state for campaign entitlement
steps: Bind the entitlement to the campaign and a proven provider subject namespace, not to a wallet/device.
Implement a unified spent claim-state with an idempotent claim ID and domain separation.
Keep the eligibility adapter provider-neutral; concrete credential validators are attached in O06.
scenarios: A concurrent claim through two gateways/wallets yields one final issuance.
A change of owner secret, salt, or policy version does not create a repeat entitlement in the same campaign.
tasks.acceptance: Replay/cross-domain restrictions are verified before connecting external providers.

tasks.title: Add immutable royalty accounting and pull payout
steps: Define the exact fee base and rounding per the manifest; separate the operator reserve from the royalty.
In the existing contract package, add a minimal splitter/vault without administrative rights for the revenue recipient.
Count a payout exactly once and allow a share to accumulate when the recipient reverts.
scenarios: The sum of all shares and the remainder equals the inflow; a repeated withdrawal does not pay twice.
Compromise of the recipient does not grant mint/pause/upgrade/blacklist/committee authority and does not block other payments.
tasks.acceptance: Role/call graph and conservation tests confirm the non-controlling share; contract addresses/bytecode are included in the manifest.

tasks.title: Pin down sufficient proof of service for claims
steps: Separate the fact of a signed receipt, actual retrieval, and the assertion of physical independence of copies.
Define the payable unit original/index/copy/repair, the admissible claimant, and the finite reserve.
Define only formalizable reject/slash cases; a missed ping is not proof of fraud.
scenarios: One real delivery with repair decomposes into services and maximum payouts.
Recipient/operator collusion does not create payouts beyond the funded pool; the residual laundering risk is measured.
tasks.acceptance: A verifiable claim contract is reconciled with real receipts and the resource model before settlement implementation.

tasks.title: Implement operator claims and settlement
steps: Accept bounded batch service proofs, verify operation/holder/epoch and the funded reserve.
Atomically mark the claim spent and pay out/accrue the admissible share accounting for royalty.
Keep retry/reorg/finality policy in the L2 adapter and show pending/finalized honestly.
scenarios: The operator is paid for original storage and admissible repair; a repeated batch is not paid.
A foreign receipt, a changed service class, an expired claim, and crash/reorg do not create a double payout/refund.
tasks.acceptance: The full delivery→repair→settlement path passes on local EVM and the chosen testnet.

tasks.title: Verify economic attacks in a single scenario set
steps: Assemble independent conservation/spent/claim oracles with concurrent spends, handover, subsidy drain, recipient revert, and reorg.
Verify finite autonomy before/after the hard lease and old retrieval during an L2 outage.
Save seeds, bytecode/config, all failed candidates, and the exact security assumptions.
scenarios: No path increases the funded transport resource or the total payout.
Several malicious RPCs do not bypass the trust model; quota exhaustion remains a bounded failure.
tasks.acceptance: The targeted economic set is green on a single revision; E19–E22 are repeated on the final RC.

tasks.title: Implement provider-neutral Credential/TrustProfile
steps: Define ExternalCredential, ProviderBinding, and TrustProfile with issuer/subject namespace, owner possession, claims, policy version, and expiry.
Separate proven account identity, voluntary trust, and eligibility for a specific funded grant.
Persist the binding separately from the root identity; do not use email/username/phone as a stable subject.
scenarios: A profile explicitly accepts only the listed issuer claims and terms.
A credential of a foreign owner/audience or a mixed policy epoch is not accepted and grants no recovery/mint authority.
tasks.acceptance: There are strict wire vectors, a storage lifecycle, and a broker boundary; login does not change the NetworkID.

tasks.title: Verify single-issuer and k-of-n attestation
steps: Support an explicit organizational 1-of-1 and a separate threshold profile with distinct signer IDs.
Tie all signatures to a single challenge, owner, claims digest, policy epoch, and upstream evidence.
The transport stake/BFT committee does not automatically appoint login attestors.
scenarios: 1-of-1 works only in the accepted scope; k-of-n requires a real threshold of distinct admissible keys.
Duplicates, different epochs/issuers, and unconfirmed claims do not add up; an outage is limited to this trust profile.
tasks.acceptance: Both variants pass independent fixtures; the UI can honestly explain their different assumptions.

tasks.title: Implement Google JWT/JWKS validation
steps: Before coding, cross-check the current official Google OAuth/OIDC documentation and the registered native client profile.
Verify the signature, admissible issuer, exact audience/authorized party, subject, nonce, expiry, and owner challenge.
Cache JWKS for an admissible term/rotation with bounded refresh; do not contact Google on every message.
scenarios: Genuine offline fixtures of the current and rotated key pass with a valid challenge.
A foreign aud, alg confusion, an expired nonce, a modified JWT, and an unknown key without admissible refresh are rejected.
tasks.acceptance: The provider-specific validator returns only verified claims for O01 and does not issue stamps itself.

tasks.title: Wire up the native Google PKCE flow
steps: Create a one-time session state/nonce/PKCE bound to the local owner and a bounded callback.
Open the system auth flow only on a user action; handle cancel/retry/timeout without losing the profile.
After token validation, persist the credential atomically and delete the temporary auth secrets.
scenarios: Real authorization yields an owner-bound credential; cancellation and retry do not change the address.
An intercepted callback/replayed code, a different state, and a parallel session do not substitute the owner.
tasks.acceptance: There is a live Google flow with a valid callback registration; unit fixtures do not close this gate.
tasks.external_dependency: A registered Google native OAuth client and a permitted test account.

tasks.title: Implement a site/org gateway with owner-bound handoff
steps: In a separate optional gateway application, implement challenge→site/OIDC auth→signed credential→daemon possession.
Keep OAuth secrets only on the gateway; allowlist issuer/origin/callback, protect discovery from SSRF.
Add a reference site issuer and a native organization-account profile; an outage does not stop the chat.
scenarios: Reference OIDC and an explicit org issuer yield verifiable claims for the intended owner.
A foreign owner, intercepted handoff, redirect/issuer substitution, and replay do not yield a credential; server tokens do not reach the desktop.
tasks.acceptance: A deployable gateway and reference site work with the shared O01/O02; no specific government system is assumed.
tasks.external_dependency: Domain/HTTPS/callback and a registered reference issuer for the live handoff; local fixtures are possible in advance.

tasks.title: Implement the Telegram gateway adapter
steps: Cross-check the current official Telegram Login/OIDC method for the chosen registration.
Verify provider evidence in the gateway and bind the handoff to owner, request digest, origin, expiry, and one-time consumption.
Return only a scoped credential; do not include the bot/client secret in the bundle or renderer.
scenarios: A real Telegram login completes with a credential for the original desktop challenge.
A foreign Telegram subject, an expired/replayed handoff, and owner substitution are rejected; a blocked bot affects only this branch.
tasks.acceptance: A live Telegram flow passes together with negative handoff cases and offline gateway control.
tasks.external_dependency: A registered Telegram bot/client, a gateway, and an explicitly permitted test account.

tasks.title: Tie credential eligibility to the funded campaign
steps: Apply the allowlisted trust-profile/version/provider namespace to a single atomic claim-state.
Deduplicate the stable subject across device/wallet/attestor; accept pairwise namespaces only with a proven mapping or a pinned sector/client.
Limit linked Google/Telegram accounts by a shared campaign cap; treat unlinked accounts as residual Sybil risk.
scenarios: One subject gets one entitlement across different wallets/devices.
A change of salt/version/attestor and cross-provider linking do not double the grant; independent identities are not automatically declared identical.
tasks.acceptance: Eligibility and the actual funded claim are separated; the cross-provider policy is verified in a concurrent flow.

tasks.title: Implement refresh/revoke/unlink without losing the address
steps: Refresh provider binding and trust/JWKS at explicit versions and terms.
Keep unlinking separate from the root, contacts, history, and the used campaign entitlement.
On an issuer/key outage, return a scoped failure; do not block saved books and ordinary communication.
scenarios: Unlink/relink and rotation preserve the NetworkID, messages, and the already used entitlement.
A changed display name/email does not grant a new entitlement; the issuer gains no ability to recover the root.
tasks.acceptance: The lifecycle is verified for Google, Telegram, and site/org without implicit profile re-creation.

tasks.title: Add an understandable funded onboarding UI
steps: Offer a key-only start and separate voluntary provider/trust branches.
Show the admissible campaign, available transport resource, TTL/limits, and the gas sponsor state; do not promise cash-out or the same bonus for any login.
Explain fund/L2/provider errors separately; keep the transition to the paid path and a working profile.
scenarios: In each permitted campaign branch, a user without a crypto balance sends the first message on real collateral.
Exhausted/cutoff/rejected credentials do not create stamps and do not delete local data.
tasks.acceptance: A headless visual/native flow covers Google/Telegram/org and the failure of each external dependency.

tasks.title: Accept the full provider/onboarding lifecycle
steps: Run a live login of the three branches, 1-of-1 and k-of-n fixtures, first funded messages, and repeated claims.
Verify cancel/retry, unlink/relink, rotation, issuer-off, and the fund after cutoff.
Save redacted evidence with the actual registrations/domains, not tokens/secrets.
scenarios: All enabled branches genuinely work without test substitution of credentials.
An unavailable registration/provider stays blocked_by_environment, not PASS and not skipped-required.
tasks.acceptance: Each of O01–O08 has its own full-scope check; live results are tied to the candidate revision.

tasks.title: Close the durable private rendezvous rotation loop
steps: Reuse Kademlia/private pointers for bounded mailbox rotation and current contact hints.
Provide reads of retained older periods without infinite slot enumeration.
Update pointers after repair/epoch change with verification of signature/domain/expiry.
scenarios: After rotation, an offline recipient discovers the live history without the sender.
Public enumeration, a stale pointer, and an unconfirmed NodeRecord do not reveal contacts or the new route.
tasks.acceptance: The rendezvous lifecycle is tied to first contact, established history, and repair, not only to DHT unit tests.

tasks.title: Find admissible surviving holders after losses
steps: Verify the current advertised-route limit: Full130 picks a survivor among four; that is not all nine losses out of ten.
Hook up the existing authenticated placement/registry discovery for the remaining admissible survivors without unbounded scanning.
When a live copy cannot be found, show the exact availability boundary; do not substitute the Full130 conditions.
scenarios: A surviving holder outside the four initial hints is discovered via a verifiable route.
A foreign placement proof and an unavailable network do not lead to a false empty/complete.
tasks.acceptance: The R10 discoverability scope is stated and verified separately from the historical Full130 fixture.

tasks.title: Close clean company-off bootstrap
steps: Gather several independent hints: invitation, cached peers, LAN where available, replaceable bootstrap/registry sources.
A new empty client must verify network/genesis/trust without relying on a single vendor endpoint.
Record the operators and failure domains of the external rig separately from the local processes.
scenarios: With company DNS/API/bootstrap turned off, the client joins via an independent invitation.
A forged registry/root/peer record is not accepted even though the endpoint is reachable.
tasks.acceptance: There is a fresh-join transcript in an independent testnet; a single laptop does not count as independent operators.
tasks.external_dependency: Reachable nodes of independent operators and an approved testnet trust manifest.

tasks.title: Accept the NAT/hole-punch/relay matrix for ordinary clients
steps: Reuse the isolated Linux/OrbStack topology; pin the NAT types and the unavailable direct path.
Verify relay replacement, possible direct upgrade, and reconnect for the packaged CLI and the desktop flow.
Preserve peer authentication/E2EE, limits, and cleanup without changing the host firewall.
scenarios: Messages and ACKs arrive through another relay after the first one is lost; a cold reconnect repeats the admissible path.
The relay sees no plaintext and does not substitute the peer; a localhost-only exchange is not passed off as NAT.
tasks.acceptance: There is real NAT/relay evidence of the ordinary adapters on the supported profiles.

tasks.title: Verify hostile peers and operator limits
steps: Assemble oversize/slow-reader/forged-record/proof cases on real TCP/Noise/QUIC peers.
Measure memory, CPU, queue, and fairness of an honest peer under the current limits.
Node mode is enabled explicitly with a disk/network/CPU/price/TTL budget; disabling preserves the obligation or an explicit drain policy.
scenarios: Honest chat keeps working under malicious peer load; resources remain bounded.
The default client does not start storing foreign data without consent; quota exhaustion does not yield a receipt.
tasks.acceptance: Operator UX/daemon policy and the actual limits agree; the current revision passes the whole targeted hostile set.

tasks.title: Show history, gaps, and recovery without false completeness
steps: Continue the existing pagination, distinguishing loaded/local/retained/complete and unavailable/expired/rejoin.
On a new pointer/epoch, update the projection without erasing already imported history.
Direct retries into the shared Core recovery; do not make UI requests that bypass paid admission.
scenarios: History of more than 1051 entries scrolls without losing position; a cold reopen shows the same messages.
A partial graph/MLS gap is not displayed as an empty completed chat.
tasks.acceptance: A person sees the reason for incompleteness and the admissible action; a native flow confirms the backend state.

tasks.title: Add local search over protected history
steps: Index only the admissible locally decrypted history inside the encrypted profile.
Update the index atomically with import/delete and request bounded pages.
After lock/recovery/version upgrade, synchronize the index without plaintext in external caches.
scenarios: Search finds the exact messages/contacts after imports and a restart.
Disk-full/rollback does not leave a search result without a message; a locked profile does not yield content.
tasks.acceptance: Search works in the ordinary UI and does not move plaintext into an unprotected DB or telemetry.

tasks.title: Wire up notifications and application lock
steps: Tie native notifications to the durable inbox, user setting, and lock state.
When locked, close renderer access to sensitive views/keys and revoke the transient UI session, preserving an explicit daemon policy.
Control preview text, sound, and navigation to the right chat without re-delivery.
scenarios: One message does not create a duplicate notification after a restart; the action opens the right conversation.
A locked preview does not show secret text; an OS permission refusal does not break delivery.
tasks.acceptance: Notifications/lock are verified on each target OS; screenshots and OS settings are not substituted by UI mocks.

tasks.title: Add backup/recovery and understandable system errors
steps: Build export/import/version warnings into the current profile flow.
Show disk-full, wrong key, failed migration, missing authority, and rejoin with a specific safe action.
Exclude silent reset and suggesting profile deletion as the routine way to restore sending.
scenarios: The user transfers a profile to a clean install and sees the saved history.
An import error preserves the old profile; an incorrect recovery does not bring back a revoked device.
tasks.acceptance: Recovery is reachable without raw RPC and internal scripts; errors match real backend results.

tasks.title: Verify XSS, malicious content, and UI accessibility
steps: Treat message/markdown/attachment previews as untrusted data in the current renderer.
Check CSP, external links, keyboard focus, labels, and error announcements in the main flows.
Take and inspect headless screenshots of all new states; the native bridge without mocks passes a bounded malicious-input scenario.
scenarios: Text instructing to reveal a key or perform a send remains message content.
XSS/unsafe URI/path does not trigger code/privileged calls; changing parameters requires a new valid action context.
tasks.acceptance: Basic user flows are accessible, contain no secret-bearing logs/previews, and pass visual inspection.

tasks.title: Extract a transport-only IPC adapter
steps: Separate Unix bind/connect/cleanup and the shared framing/owner-token/signed-agent checks.
Keep a single dispatcher/Core writer; remove cfg(unix) only after an equivalent platform implementation appears.
First verify concurrent clients, an oversized frame, cancel/shutdown, and a second-daemon conflict on the existing Unix path.
scenarios: The owner and a real signed agent pass through the shared broker after the refactor.
A wrong token, revoked grant, and stale session do not work; cancellation does not permit a late side effect.
tasks.acceptance: The Unix regression is green; the transport was not replaced by HTTP and does not duplicate application rules.

tasks.title: Add private Windows named pipes
steps: Implement a local-only named pipe with an ACL for the needed user and a stable profile endpoint.
Preserve the single-instance lock, shutdown, endpoint cleanup, and reconnect semantics.
Run real cross-user/remote rejection tests on Windows; do not treat a fake ACL as proof.
scenarios: Two admissible clients talk to one daemon; a cold restart frees the endpoint.
Another local user, a remote pipe, and a second daemon do not get access.
tasks.acceptance: A real Windows runtime/IPC works with verified ACLs and shared auth tests.
tasks.external_dependency: A Windows x64 runner with separate test users.

tasks.title: Port the safe materialization of credentials and sidecars
steps: Make private atomic credential creation/read with verification of opened-file identity on Windows.
Reconcile the .exe suffix, paths with spaces, bundled sidecars, and the exact provisioning commands.
Verify cold read, replacements, and symlink/reparse risks through the existing private-handle policy.
scenarios: CLI/MCP from the actual provisioning response run and use the correct seed after a restart.
A public or substituted file is rejected; an atomic replace error does not leave half the credentials.
tasks.acceptance: Windows CLI/MCP/desktop bootstrap passes without Unix-only path assumptions.
tasks.external_dependency: A Windows x64 runner; ordinary system keystores are verified in an isolated test session.

tasks.title: Build debug/e2e and shipping artifacts per platform
steps: Separate platform-specific build/packaging in the existing scripts/build-desktop.mjs and CI adapters.
For native automation, provide a temporary debug/e2e keystore on Windows/Linux and its absence in shipping features.
Build the macOS app, Windows installer, and Linux package with real CLI/MCP/skill resources and pinned lockfiles.
scenarios: A clean install on each OS contains working sidecars and a compatible profile.
The release dependency graph contains no test plugin, dev server, OAuth secret, or test crypto.
tasks.acceptance: The three installer artifacts have hashes, feature manifests, and noninteractive test-key cleanup.
tasks.external_dependency: Three native runners; signing/notarization credentials available for the corresponding release stage.

tasks.title: Implement voluntary updates and upgrade compatibility
steps: Verify the signature/version of the update manifest and the user's explicit consent to install.
Keep the old working artifact/profile until a successful admissible upgrade.
A missing release CDN does not block the installed application; an unsupported downgrade does not write the new schema.
scenarios: A previous-compatible client upgrades with identity/history/inbox without losses.
A substituted update, user refusal, and power loss do not turn the profile empty and do not require a mandatory update.
tasks.acceptance: The voluntary update/rollback policy is confirmed on three OSes and does not give the vendor the right to disable the chat.

tasks.title: Verify clean install, key store, and native production smoke
steps: Install each shipping artifact on a clean OS, create an identity without OAuth, send/receive a message, restart.
Separately verify the instrumented real bridge and the shipping artifact without instrumentation.
Inspect screenshots, check the privacy of files/keystore, and delete the test profiles after stopping the processes.
scenarios: Identity and history are preserved; bundled CLI/MCP run from the installed path.
Missing permissions/key access give an explicit error without fallback to plaintext; automation does not trigger a login Keychain prompt.
tasks.acceptance: All three OSes have their own actual evidence; cross-compilation and a macOS smoke do not close Windows.

tasks.title: Assemble the full V1 wire/crypto compatibility corpus
steps: Consolidate identity/grant/message/control/history/attachment/credential/public-postage/current-and-legacy vectors for the V1 scope only.
Verify golden bytes/hashes/signatures with a second codec/oracle or upstream vectors; encode→decode of one's own code is not enough.
Pin the unknown critical/noncritical extension policy and different domains/epochs.
scenarios: Two compatible client versions read the same V1 objects on three OSes.
Unknown critical, domain substitution, and an altered signature are rejected; an unsupported adapter is not called paid/verified.
tasks.acceptance: Every V1 wire family has an independent positive/negative vector and a version policy.

tasks.title: Pin down the independent testnet and external prerequisites
steps: Record chain/genesis/bytecode, checkpoint profile, admissible operators/attestors, seeds/relays, and failure domains.
Separate the counts of keys, processes, machines, organizations, and trust administrators.
Verify replacement sources for the company and the absence of a mandatory revenue/gateway/CDN for the already working network.
scenarios: An independent operator reproduces join/serve/retrieve with the published configuration.
Several processes of the project owner do not count as an independent quorum; an unavailable live resource is marked blocked.
tasks.acceptance: The testnet manifest and accesses are ready for the full RC; admission of mainnet money is not implied.
tasks.external_dependency: Independent operators, testnet funding, provider registrations, native runners, and signing setup.

tasks.title: Assemble the full runner across 11 suites and 22 cases
steps: Use the existing check scripts and scenario adapters; add the missing manifest/aggregation without a parallel test system.
Verify exact revision/lock/config/binary/oracle hashes, non-zero counts, and the absence of missing/skipped-required.
Run the full suite only after the functional tasks are done; do not assume the cargo xtask commands from the old plan exist.
scenarios: A fake/stale/missing PASS report does not close the RC.
Every required case is genuinely selected, a child failure is not lost, and cleanup is preserved on stop.
tasks.acceptance: There is one exact command/manifest for the final run, separate native/production/live results, and a list of platform gates.

tasks.title: Freeze the release candidate and verify launch readiness
steps: Pin the commit, clean source set, locks, schema/wire versions, bytecode/genesis/config, and the hashes of the three install artifacts.
Verify the presence of accepted backend test reviews for the new features and all external prerequisites.
Produce an immutable run manifest for the following 22 cases; forbid source/config edits during the run.
scenarios: A mismatch of any mandatory artifact or an unready OS stops the corresponding gate with an explicit status.
A historical Full130/871-workspace pass does not carry over automatically to the new RC.
tasks.acceptance: The RC is prepared for shared acceptance; product_validated remains false until all gates complete.

tasks.title: Run all mandatory suites on the RC
steps: Run the full V03 runner: backend unit/integration, frontend, wire/crypto, simulation, contracts/proofs, CLI/MCP, and platform checks.
Reconcile non-zero counts, accepted reviews, and exact hashes before/after; account for heavy legacy targets separately but do not skip the mandatory ones.
Save failed/skipped/missing as blocking states; after a fix, repeat the affected gates and the overall RC on a new revision.
scenarios: All 11 required suite IDs have an actual result on the accepted set of inputs.
A flaky/quarantined required test or an unexecuted live/native case is not hidden by an overall PASS.
tasks.acceptance: The overall run is green; the 22 E2E below and the native matrix are additionally mandatory if the same runner did not execute them.

tasks.title: Run a 24-hour process soak and benchmark
steps: Run real client/node processes for 24 hours per the C04 manifest, separately from the virtual-clock tests.
Include 10,000 duplicate/reorder messages and the accepted group/attachment/NAT loads; measure accepted/completed/errors, p50/p95/p99, CPU/RAM/disk/queues.
Verify bounded growth, cold restart, absence of leaks, and the exact content of the received messages; save the original thresholds before the run.
