scenarios: All messages accepted in the manifest are recovered under the stated conditions without duplicates.
A fast rejected/timeout is not counted as successful delivery; a simulation of a day does not replace 24 hours of wall time.
tasks.acceptance: On the unchanged RC there is long process evidence and a benchmark against the accepted profile; exceeding resources/losses blocks the final acceptance.

tasks.title: Clean install and own identity
steps: On clean macOS/Windows/Linux, create a profile without OAuth, exchange the first message, close and reopen the application.
Verify the NetworkID, exact message contents, keystore, and the real UI→Rust→daemon path.
scenarios: Neither a Google login nor public keys in the renderer are needed for one's own address.
Wrong key/permission failures do not create a new empty profile.
tasks.acceptance: Identity and history are preserved on each OS; the shipping artifact is verified separately from debug.

tasks.title: Company-off fresh join
steps: Disable company bootstrap/DNS/API; remove cached peers for a new client.
Join via an independent invitation and verify the authenticated registry/trust.
scenarios: Connectivity and network verification work through independent available sources.
A forged root/record is not accepted even from a reachable bootstrap.
tasks.acceptance: There is a clean-join transcript and a manifest of real independent operators.

tasks.title: NAT and relay loss
steps: In a real isolated NAT topology, run a desktop and packaged CLI exchange without a direct path.
Remove the active relay; verify replacement, restart, and an admissible direct upgrade.
scenarios: The original payload/ACK reach the addressee after the switch.
The relay reveals no content and does not substitute the authenticated peer.
tasks.acceptance: NAT profiles and network faults are observed in fact; a localhost smoke is not used as a replacement.

tasks.title: Hostile peer and backpressure
steps: Send forged records/proofs, oversized frames, and slow-reader traffic to a real peer.
Simultaneously run an honest exchange and measure memory/CPU/queues/latency.
scenarios: The honest peer progresses within the established limits.
A bad proof does not save paid state; exceeding quotas does not bypass admission.
tasks.acceptance: Limits and fairness are confirmed on the RC without increasing them in the test.

tasks.title: Offline/crash/dedup and full history
steps: Run the unchanged Full130 with sender absent, real copy loss, both SQL faults, and a cold full graph.
Separately pass first-offline Welcome, reorder/duplicate, and several MLS epochs through ordinary entry points.
scenarios: One exact MessageID per original, the full plaintext oracle, and partial129→full130 before the earliest expiry.
No substitution of the full import by merging two caches, raising the TTL, or a manual Welcome.
tasks.acceptance: The long established history and the first offline contact are closed; legacy/gap/rejoin limits are explicitly verified.

tasks.title: Operator-only repair 10→7→10
steps: Reach ten valid data/index copies; stop both clients and three assigned nodes.
Allow spares, wait for autonomous repair, read the new bytes with an independent audit client, and bring Bob back.
scenarios: Hashes, new receipts/locations, and the finite budget all agree.
Without spare/capacity the status stays degraded; the sender does not sign repairs in the background.
tasks.acceptance: The repair is performed by the network with proven discoverability; separate identities are not passed off as physical independence.

tasks.title: Index loss, chunks, TTL, and disk-full
steps: Lose an available index holder and part of the attachment chunks; recover via another route and resume.
Reach expiry and disk-full in separate branches; verify retention and GC.
scenarios: Before the term, the exact hash of the whole file is restored.
Expired/quota/disk-full do not become delivered and do not delete still-live paid objects.
tasks.acceptance: Success and refusals are verified on actual bytes, usage rows, and restart.

tasks.title: Group and the boundaries of old/new secrets
steps: Create a group, connect devices, exchange messages, exclude Bob, and add a new participant.
Verify both privacy profiles and the decryption of old/new epochs on separate real devices.
scenarios: The remaining participants read the new message.
A removed device cannot read the new epoch; a new participant does not get old secrets without a separate history-share.
tasks.acceptance: The UI roster matches the final MLS state; the declared metadata boundaries are respected.

tasks.title: Concurrent encrypted group control
steps: Create conflicting Add/Remove/Update on one parent and split the 4/3 committee 2/2.
Restore the network; enable withheld and semantically invalid MLS payload cases.
scenarios: One final prefix/roster after recovery; deterministic reject/no-op for inadmissible control.
The quorum is not lowered, keys are not rolled back, a missing payload is not finalized.
tasks.acceptance: Consensus and MLS semantics are verified independently and converge in a real client.

tasks.title: Offline device, control loss, and safe rejoin
steps: Leave a device offline longer than the key window, lose part of the control log, and restore an old backup on another device.
Verify retained catch-up, an explicit gap, and the permitted rejoin with a new MLS identity.
scenarios: The permitted history and current membership are preserved.
A revoked device does not regain rights; old private keys are not published for the sake of recovery.
tasks.acceptance: The loss of all retained records is honestly visible; recovery does not clone active ratchets.

tasks.title: Shipped CLI skill, MCP, and a real host
steps: On the installed artifact, the host performs identity/send/delivery/poll/ack for a new contact, then a restart.
An independent MCP client verifies the wire lifecycle/tools/resources/scopes; repeat the exchange behind NAT/relay.
scenarios: CLI works without MCP and without sources; the MCP stdout contains only protocol.
Bad scope, stale grant, and an incompatible protocol get an explicit refusal.
tasks.acceptance: There are real host and NAT transcripts, stable JSON/exit codes, and a preserved inbox.

tasks.title: Injection, XSS, and revocation between prepare/send
steps: Deliver untrusted markdown/attachment/message asking to reveal a secret/send a message.
Revoke a grant after preparing an action; change the parameters of an already approved action.
scenarios: Ordinary permitted correspondence continues.
The renderer executes no XSS; the broker reveals no key and accepts no old approval or revoked actor.
tasks.acceptance: Forbidden side effects are verified by the actual outbox/recipient, not a single error text.

tasks.title: Live Google OAuth lifecycle
steps: Run a genuine native PKCE login, cancel/retry, and JWKS/key rotation in the permitted mode.
Unlink the provider, restart the application, and continue the correspondence.
scenarios: The credential is bound to the original owner; the address and history are preserved.
Wrong state/audience/nonce and replay do not create a binding/grant.
tasks.acceptance: A real registration is used; fixtures complement rather than replace the live flow.

tasks.title: Telegram and site/org handoff
steps: Run a live Telegram and reference site OIDC; verify the 1-of-1 and k-of-n accepted profiles.
Substitute owner/handoff/origin, then shut down the issuer/gateway and continue the existing chat.
scenarios: Correct scoped credentials are accepted by the original owner.
Interception does not grant rights to another profile; client secrets stay only in the gateway.
tasks.acceptance: An issuer outage is limited to new credentials; messages/history keep working.

tasks.title: A genuinely backed free start
steps: From a profile without crypto balance, obtain a permitted funded grant and send a message.
Repeat the claim across device/wallet/attestor/providers; exhaust the fund and pass the cutoff.
scenarios: One entitlement is not doubled; spending is bounded by the real funded balance.
Invalid eligibility, another namespace, and an empty fund do not create stamps; the paid path works after cutoff.
tasks.acceptance: Receipts, campaign policy, and the conservation oracle are preserved; a monetary cash-out is not promised.

tasks.title: Concurrent spend, handover, refund, and payout
steps: Spend one stamp concurrently through different admissible nodes, including crash/retry and handover.
Finish the claims/refund paths for the same operation and repeat after a cold restart.
scenarios: One final operation-bound spend and no more than one admissible payout/refund.
A change of epoch/format/node does not create a new resource or an empty spent namespace.
tasks.acceptance: An independent oracle confirms global spent and conservation on the full trace.

tasks.title: Reorg and finite L2 autonomy
steps: Feed a false RPC/root, a real admissible reorg, and an outage before/after the hard lease.
Verify automatic renewal, pending inputs, and historical retrieval with expired admissions.
scenarios: New spending is admissible only within the lease; old live objects are read by historical proof.
Non-final funding does not become a balance; after hard expiry, admission waits.
tasks.acceptance: Trust/signatures, expiry, and availability are separated; renewal does not require a manual QC install.

tasks.title: Royalty conservation and the absence of governance
steps: Perform the fee split/operator settlement, then repeat the payout and revert the revenue recipient.
Verify the full role/call graph and attempts of a captured revenue key to govern the network.
scenarios: Sums are preserved; a blocked share is available via pull payment and does not interfere with the rest.
There is no mint/pause/upgrade/blacklist/committee right and no repeated payout.
tasks.acceptance: Bytecode/config and the independent model agree; revenue-off does not disable the transport.

tasks.title: Everyday UX and local storage secrecy
steps: Run search, send/download attachment, notifications, lock, backup/import, and disk-full/restart.
Check the chosen WAL/temp/log/preview surfaces for sensitive content and compare the restored history.
scenarios: Message/file state is consistent; errors give a specific action.
Plaintext does not appear in the checked unprotected artifacts; backup does not restore revoked rights.
tasks.acceptance: Native UI evidence and a check of the actual data confirm all branches.

tasks.title: Native installer and production smoke on three OSes
steps: Install the exact RC artifacts on macOS ARM64, Windows x64, and Linux x64.
Verify the real bridge, keystore, restart, packaged CLI/MCP, and separately the shipping feature set; inspect screenshots.
scenarios: All platforms pass on their own, without replacing a cross-compilation report.
The shipping artifact contains no test plugins/debug crypto/dev server; native automation does not touch the login Keychain.
tasks.acceptance: Three standalone install/smoke reports are tied to the same source/lock/config inputs.

tasks.title: Two compatible versions and extension boundaries
steps: Exchange identity/mailbox/history/attachments between the previous-compatible and current releases.
Connect a test settlement/verifier adapter and pass unknown critical/noncritical extensions.
scenarios: Shared V1 data is read without loss and without a silent migration reset.
Unknown critical is rejected; an unsupported adapter does not declare unverified payment as verified.
tasks.acceptance: The compatibility corpus and real processes agree; jobs/reviews are not included back into V1.

tasks.title: The whole network without company resources
steps: On an independent network, disable company endpoints, gateway, release CDN, and the revenue recipient.
Continue DM/group/CLI/MCP, retrieval, and operator repair under the declared surviving copies/retention/budget/connectivity.
Separately verify a clean join via independent hints.
scenarios: Installed clients and custodians continue the permitted operations.
New external credentials are not imitated; expiry/resource exhaustion are shown honestly.
tasks.acceptance: Failure domains and external faults are confirmed; the existence of ten keys is not by itself proof of decentralization.

tasks.title: Accept the 67 cards and close AR1–AR5 on evidence
steps: For each source card, verify the entire remaining scope, its dependency GREEN, and real test/demo artifacts; a link to a single plan task does not mean acceptance.
Reconcile all AR findings: fixes or documented preservation of the protecting invariants, without a hidden preview scope.
Match 67 task acceptances, 22 E2E, 11 suites, and 3 OSes to a single RC; repeat the security-sensitive review by an independent reviewer.
scenarios: Missing/skipped-required/blocked/flaky or a different revision block full readiness.
A sum of old successful runs does not substitute for current evidence.
tasks.acceptance: Only with the complete set can product_validated=true be set for V1 code/testnet; mainnet_transport_approved remains a separate decision.

tasks.title: Prepare the delivery and the final report
steps: Assemble checksums, install/update instructions, the CLI skill, testnet manifest, compatibility/migration notes, and security limitations.
Prepare the concrete release artifact and changelog from the final implementation, preserving the evidence and the former failures.
Finish cleanup of processes/temporary profiles and hand the results to the user; perform external publication only within a separate assignment.
scenarios: Another user reproduces the installation and the start of a conversation from the documentation.
Secrets, native test keys, output caches, and local configs are not included in the delivery.
tasks.acceptance: A verifiable V1 code/testnet package is ready. This plan itself does not launch publication or deployment.
